scope: Flood source/mechanism evidence and compatible-input screening scenario; no calibrated flood risk model.

scenario.interpretation: Treat available inputs as time-compatible for the requested scenario. Dates remain recorded and no event-calibration claim follows from this assumption.
scenario.rainfall_role: Real27June2025 daily rain is compatible scenario rainfall context at its native coverage/resolution; it is not a recovered2021 event hyetograph, short-duration intensity or return-period storm.

api_schema.source_id: Stable ID within its named dataset; never join API549 to ArcGIS310 by OID alone.
api_schema.confidence_semantics: Documented: explicit applicable source classification, without independent accuracy/probability claim. Unknown: absent or not assignable to this geometry. Qualitative narrative interpretation is stored separately with its basis.
api_schema.reported_source_types: All explicitly coded source categories, preserved alongside narrative review.
api_schema.mechanism_basis: Traceable source-field or scoped narrative basis.
api_schema.observation_date: ISO calendar date if source supplies it, otherwise null plus precision label.
api_schema.scenario_temporal_assumption: time-compatible, at user direction; original dates remain visible.
api_schema.priority_attention: Separate documented-history/official-assessment category; numeric terrain metrics remain independently inspectable.

refinement_rules: Use explicit history and official-assessment category overrides at their actual polygons, preserving raw terrainP/C/S and source factors. Do not silently assign100 or arbitrary score floors.
History overrides have precedence in attention display if a terrain model misses a real observation, but they do not establish recurrence, current depth, cause or guaranteed future flooding.
Assessment high/medium/low are supplier ordinal labels only; classify by highest overlapping supplier level without interpreting it as a locally calibrated probability.
Keep text reports searchable with exact source row and original description; no fabricated point/address match, district fill or ad-hoc buffer.
Show river reaches and schematic area points as context only; neither defines a flood width or pixel-level override.
Use actual cadastral footprints for overlap/exposure and planform context. Floor counts are not heights and outlines do not supply sill levels, openings, basement entry or drainage barriers.
Use archived sewer/green geometry as context. Do not infer operating capacity from line proximity or perviousness from green-area membership.
Preserve open-water land exclusions, NoData, upstream boundary uncertainty and source dates; historical/official evidence can still be shown where the terrain score is unknown.
Do not fit weights or choose cutoffs from incomplete mixed-source positives without surveyed negatives and a documented sampling frame.

Next physical-model stage needs timed rainfall/loss scenarios, corrected routing/culverts and building pathways, measured or explicitly scenario drainage, plus independent event validation. UK/Scottish coefficients are examples, not Sofia defaults.

primary_sources.finding: Source, mechanism and flood characteristic are separate and may have multiple entries; restriction can apply to a sewer or river; flash characteristic is not a pluvial-source synonym.
136 mapped drone-survey zones; source year2021, month discrepancy preserved.
January2021 mapped northern flooding after heavy rain in river corridors; study-level evidence cannot identify each polygon cause.
Rainfall, river and artificial water-bearing infrastructure are distinct source categories, separate from blockage/overtopping mechanisms and flash/snowmelt characteristics.
Use observed history to investigate missed flooding, drainage and other-source interactions; lack of past observation does not prove safety. Coupled sewer/surface/river models address interactions.
Operational hazard mapping models rainfall/runoff, drainage and terrain and uses local review; its country-specific parameters are not Sofia calibrations.
Risk involves hazard, exposure, vulnerability and capacity; footprint overlap alone does not estimate loss.
